# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 91 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 91 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_091_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 8

**1** "The ninth mountain, which was utterly barren and inhabited by serpents — these are those who believed but were stained with many kinds of sins; they were neither consistently repentant nor attached to the saints. **2** Therefore many of them are hollow, for having committed many sins they are empty within; some of them never repented at all. **3** You saw the serpents? These are their sins embedded within them, devouring them and destroying them. For such people their very lives are destroyed, along with their households." **4** "The tenth mountain with great spreading trees casting shade all around, with cattle resting and ruminating beneath them — these are those who believed and are very blessed; they never stray from God but abide in him always with joy, meditating on the Lord and his truth, having deep roots in God." **5** "The eleventh mountain where the trees were laden with various fruits — these are those who suffered for the name of the Lord, enduring all afflictions gladly and cheerfully, giving up their own lives." **6** "The twelfth mountain, which was white — these are the infants and those whose minds are pure, who never harbored an evil thought, who never knew what wickedness was, but always remained in innocence." **7** "For these reasons the mountains are different and varied, because these peoples differ from one another; and for each of them a particular repentance has been appointed, so that whoever among them repents shall live unto God — provided they repent before the tower is finished. **8** But if the tower is completed before they repent, they shall have no place in the tower; only those fitted in before the tower is completed shall have a place in it."

---

### Translator's Note
The twelve-mountain typology concludes with a powerful eschatological warning (vv. 7-8): repentance has a deadline. The tower's completion = the end of the age. This is the pastoral core of the entire Shepherd of Hermas — repentance is available, but not indefinitely. Mountain 12's white innocence (infants) forms a perfect ring-composition with Mountain 1's black apostasy. SOPHIA follows LOGOS throughout.
